cases.name: Correct swapped relationship allow-lists
cases.trap: A loaded profile and a readable inverse can conceal source/target allow-lists swapped against the written Markdown link. Cases specify expected responses, not recorded ablation results.
cases.prompt: Accepted content: requirement.md (type: requirement) links to anchor.md (type: anchor) under Derived from. The profile loads with inverse derives but allowed_source_types: [anchor] and allowed_target_types: [requirement]. Assess formatting, then show the corrected representation and a valid near-miss check inline.
expectations: Identify requirement as link-containing source and anchor as linked target
Flag both swapped lists; correct to source [requirement] and target [anchor]
Keep forward constraints unchanged when querying incoming derives
Check exact frontmatter values; Requirement or a concept alias is not requirement
Distinguish expected graph type warnings from document conformance without claiming unexecuted checks
negative_expectations: Approve swapped lists because the inverse reads anchor derives requirement
Decide whether the requirement is substantively justified
Claim profile loading proves type compatibility

cases.name: Select the checked node for incoming invariants
cases.trap: The invariant field source_type looks like the edge source selector, and the displayed inverse looks like the counting relationship.
cases.prompt: Accepted obligation: each anchor must have an incoming derived-from link from a requirement. requirement.md links to anchor.md. The invariant uses source_type: requirement, relationship: derives, direction: incoming, min: 1, max: -1. Show the corrected representation inline without inventing obligations.
expectations: Select anchor with source_type because it is the checked node
Use forward relationship derived-from for incoming counts
Keep allowed_source_types [requirement] and allowed_target_types [anchor]
Show the expected valid anchor incoming count and a missing-link case
negative_expectations: Select requirement merely because the field is named source_type
Use displayed inverse derives as the invariant relationship
Reverse the written Markdown link to make the rule pass

cases.name: Repair the observed profile schema failure
cases.trap: Observed repository incident: explicit profile loading failed because requirement-has-source omitted relationship, used incoming despite its outgoing description, and max:null with min:1. CLI conformance success concealed missing graph enforcement; this is incident lineage, not an ablation result.
cases.prompt: Our documentation says OKF validation passes but the requirement links are untyped. The requirement-has-source invariant omits relationship, uses incoming despite its accepted outgoing-source description, and has max:null with min:1. Explain how to configure the repository profile from the existing relationships, showing corrected fields inline and the checks needed before claiming success.
expectations: Identify the selected profile and server capabilities as evidence to inspect
Derive fields from accepted outgoing-source obligation
Use explicit relationship and intentional unlimited bound
Require observed profile loading and graph checks before claiming verified enforcement
negative_expectations: Claim no profile support from an older checkout
Treat CLI conformance success as graph enforcement
Invent relationships just to make coverage pass

cases.name: Detect incomplete index inventory despite validation
cases.trap: A green reserved-file validator is mistaken for proof that index.md inventories every owned document.
cases.prompt: a.md and b.md belong to the bundle. index.md has no frontmatter and links only a.md. validate_doc reports no index errors. Is its structure conformant?
expectations: Flag b.md missing from the applicable index inventory despite validator success
negative_expectations: Approve index completeness from validator success

cases.name: Detect stale log currency
cases.trap: Valid Log metadata and chronological ordering are mistaken for a current entry documenting today's change.
cases.prompt: Today a.md changed. log.md has valid Log frontmatter and ordered entries but only an entry from yesterday. Assess formatting and show the needed correction inline.
expectations: Flag absent current-date entry for a.md
Show the applicable edit timestamp update without rewriting historical entries
negative_expectations: Claim date-order notification checks log currency

cases.name: Keep nested bundle and native skill metadata distinct
cases.trap: Flattening nested ownership or treating native skill metadata as OKF frontmatter can produce a superficially green but incorrect inventory.
cases.prompt: Parent docs and nested child docs each have an index. Show inline how to add a native SKILL.md with name/description beside its reference material and explain the formatting checks.
expectations: Resolve parent/child ownership before inventory checks
Keep native skill metadata separate from OKF document frontmatter
Scope validation of intentionally published reference documents to their own bundle
negative_expectations: Flatten every child document into the parent index
Force type into native SKILL.md to silence a wrongly scoped validator

cases.name: Keep formatting assessment out of substantive review
cases.trap: Formatting success is promoted to architectural approval, or formatting review silently rewrites accepted substantive meaning.
cases.prompt: Formatting, index coverage, current log and profile checks are correct, but this architectural argument seems technically wrong. Explain the boundary of the OKF formatting assessment.
expectations: Assess structural conformance only
Report substantive correctness as outside this assessment
negative_expectations: Approve the architectural claim from green formatting checks
Rewrite its substantive meaning during formatting review

cases.name: Author portably with unavailable runtime tooling
cases.trap: A portable installation depends on source-repository paths or invents successful validation when MCP is unavailable.
cases.prompt: Explain how to install this skill in a different repository with no source checkout and an unavailable MCP server, then show an OKF document inline. Explain which target rules and inventory you need and what remains unverified.
expectations: Resolve direct references from the skill directory
Use target repository rules and local inventory
Mark runtime verification unproven
negative_expectations: Require implementation paths in the authoring source repo
